 Cette collection contient des registres paroissiaux et d'autres enregistrements paroissiaux provenant de diverses églises situées aux Québec.   
 Plusieurs points sont à surveiller lorsque vous consultez ces registres. Par exemple, sachez que les confessions religieuses peuvent changer. Les enregistrements de l'Église luthérienne se trouvent parfois dans des registres anglicans, alors que des enregistrements des Églises presbytérienne et méthodiste se trouvent assez fréquemment dans les registres des nouvelles confessions appartenant aujourd'hui à l'Église Unie du Canada. Veuillez noter également que la délimitation des paroisses peut parfois être modifiée, de sorte que certaines communautés peuvent avoir été desservies par différentes églises paroissiales.  French Description Government registration of vital statistics (baptism, marriage and death) did not begin until the late 1800s. For the time period prior to that, records of local churches are the chief source for vital statistics.   
 In this collection can be found parish registers and other church records from various churches in the province of Quebec.   
 There are many points to note when using these registers. For instance, be aware that denominations can change. Lutheran records, for example, may sometimes be found in Anglican registers, while Presbyterian and Methodist records are now frequently found with those of successor congregations belonging to the United Church of Canada.  What is Genealogy Quebec?

Genealogy Quebec is a subscription-based genealogy research platform that helps you trace your family history in Quebec (and beyond). It brings many collections together in one place and helps you find ancestors faster with a powerful search engine, helpful filters, and access to original record images when available.  
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 What are the kinds of tools and documents available on Genealogy Quebec?

On Genealogy Quebec, you can access a wide range of historical and genealogical records, including:

*   Parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials)
*   Birth, marriage, and death records
*   Census records
*   Obituaries and death notices
*   Gravestones and memorial cards
*   Notarial records (contracts, wills, and more)
*   City directories and reference indexes
*   Postcards and other archival materials
*   And various other kinds of historical archives

All collections are searchable through our search engine and filters, with access to record images when available.   
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 I don’t speak french. Can I still use the website?

Genealogy Quebec is designed to be used by both French and English speakers. The entire website is available in English, from the menus to the tutorials to the various search engines and databases. Most original documents will only be available in their original language, but they will often be accompanied by a readout of the important information contained in the record, which is available in both French and English.

 What is Genealogy Quebec?

Genealogy Quebec is a subscription-based genealogy research platform that helps you trace your family history in Quebec (and beyond). It brings many collections together in one place and helps you find ancestors faster with a powerful search engine, helpful filters, and access to original record images when available.  
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 What are the kinds of tools and documents available on Genealogy Quebec?

On Genealogy Quebec, you can access a wide range of historical and genealogical records, including:

*   Parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials)
*   Birth, marriage, and death records
*   Census records
*   Obituaries and death notices
*   Gravestones and memorial cards
*   Notarial records (contracts, wills, and more)
*   City directories and reference indexes
*   Postcards and other archival materials
*   And various other kinds of historical archives

All collections are searchable through our search engine and filters, with access to record images when available.   
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 I don’t speak french. Can I still use the website?

Genealogy Quebec is designed to be used by both French and English speakers. The entire website is available in English, from the menus to the tutorials to the various search engines and databases. Most original documents will only be available in their original language, but they will often be accompanied by a readout of the important information contained in the record, which is available in both French and English.

# Généalogie Québec

Provides access to over 42,000,000 images and files from the origins of New France to today, drawn from the search tools of the Drouin Genealogical Institute. Includes baptism and death certificates (1621-1849), the Fond Drouin registries from 1621 to 1967, and marriage and death certificates (1926-1997). Many digital documents are also available, such as notarized contracts, post cards, censuses, etc.

This product is limited to 10 simultaneous users. Please log in to PRDH separately if you would like to use materials linked to both databases.

The **1961 Canadian census** was a detailed enumeration of the [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada") population. Census day was June 16, 1961. On that day, Statistics Canada attempted to count every person in Canada. The total population count of Canada was 18,238,247. This was a 13.4% increase over the 1956 census of 16,080,791.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-1)

The previous census was the [1956 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Canadian_census "1956 Canadian census") and the following census was the [1966 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Canadian_census "1966 Canadian census"). This was the first census since [1901](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1901_Canadian_census "1901 Canadian census") in which all then-admitted provinces recorded a population of at least 100,000, and the last in which [Saskatchewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saskatchewan "Saskatchewan") had a larger population than neighbouring [Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba "Manitoba").

A different definition for the Northwest Territories disregards areas not included within the [Mackenzie River Electoral District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mackenzie_River_(electoral_district) "Mackenzie River (electoral district)"). If such areas were excluded, the Northwest Territories had 14,895 people in 1961 and 12,492 people in 1956.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-2) Under this definition, the Northwest Territories saw an increase of 2,403 people, or 19.2%.

The **1961 Canadian census** was a detailed enumeration of the [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada") population. Census day was June 16, 1961. On that day, Statistics Canada attempted to count every person in Canada. The total population count of Canada was 18,238,247. This was a 13.4% increase over the 1956 census of 16,080,791.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-1)

The previous census was the [1956 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Canadian_census "1956 Canadian census") and the following census was the [1966 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_Canadian_census "1966 Canadian census"). This was the first census since [1901](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1901_Canadian_census "1901 Canadian census") in which all then-admitted provinces recorded a population of at least 100,000, and the last in which [Saskatchewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saskatchewan "Saskatchewan") had a larger population than neighbouring [Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba "Manitoba").

A different definition for the Northwest Territories disregards areas not included within the [Mackenzie River Electoral District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mackenzie_River_(electoral_district) "Mackenzie River (electoral district)"). If such areas were excluded, the Northwest Territories had 14,895 people in 1961 and 12,492 people in 1956.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Canadian_census#cite_note-2) Under this definition, the Northwest Territories saw an increase of 2,403 people, or 19.2%.

 French Description Government registration of vital statistics (baptism, marriage and death) did not begin until the late 1800s. For the time period prior to that, records of local churches are the chief source for vital statistics.   
 In this collection can be found parish registers and other church records from various churches in the province of Quebec.   
 There are many points to note when using these registers. For instance, be aware that denominations can change. Lutheran records, for example, may sometimes be found in Anglican registers, while Presbyterian and Methodist records are now frequently found with those of successor congregations belonging to the United Church of Canada. Note also that parish boundaries can change, so that settlements may be served by different parish churches.   
 Le gouvernement n'a commencé à enregistrer les statistiques de l'état civil (baptêmes, mariages, décès) qu'à la fin du XIXe siècle. Pour les années antérieures, les registres tenus par les églises paroissiales constituent la principale source pour l   
 Cette collection contient des registres paroissiaux et d'autres enregistrements paroissiaux provenant de diverses églises situées aux Québec.   
 Plusieurs points sont à surveiller lorsque vous consultez ces registres. Par exemple, sachez que les confessions religieuses peuvent changer. Les enregistrements de l'Église luthérienne se trouvent parfois dans des registres anglicans, alors que des enregistrements des Églises presbytérienne et méthodiste se trouvent assez fréquemment dans les registres des nouvelles confessions appartenant aujourd'hui à l'Église Unie du Canada. Veuillez noter également que la délimitation des paroisses peut parfois être modifiée, de sorte que certaines communautés peuvent avoir été desservies par différentes églises paroissiales.  French Description Government registration of vital statistics (baptism, marriage and death) did not begin until the late 1800s. For the time period prior to that, records of local churches are the chief source for vital statistics.   
 In this collection can be found parish registers and other church records from various churches in the province of Quebec.   
 There are many points to note when using these registers. For instance, be aware that denominations can change. Lutheran records, for example, may sometimes be found in Anglican registers, while Presbyterian and Methodist records are now frequently found with those of successor congregations belonging to the United Church of Canada. Note also that parish boundaries can change, so that settlements may be served by different parish churches.

 Cette collection contient des registres paroissiaux et d'autres enregistrements paroissiaux provenant de diverses églises situées aux Québec.   
 Plusieurs points sont à surveiller lorsque vous consultez ces registres. Par exemple, sachez que les confessions religieuses peuvent changer. Les enregistrements de l'Église luthérienne se trouvent parfois dans des registres anglicans, alors que des enregistrements des Églises presbytérienne et méthodiste se trouvent assez fréquemment dans les registres des nouvelles confessions appartenant aujourd'hui à l'Église Unie du Canada. Veuillez noter également que la délimitation des paroisses peut parfois être modifiée, de sorte que certaines communautés peuvent avoir été desservies par différentes églises paroissiales.  What is Genealogy Quebec?

Genealogy Quebec is a subscription-based genealogy research platform that helps you trace your family history in Quebec (and beyond). It brings many collections together in one place and helps you find ancestors faster with a powerful search engine, helpful filters, and access to original record images when available.  
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 What are the kinds of tools and documents available on Genealogy Quebec?

On Genealogy Quebec, you can access a wide range of historical and genealogical records, including:

*   Parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials)
*   Birth, marriage, and death records
*   Census records
*   Obituaries and death notices
*   Gravestones and memorial cards
*   Notarial records (contracts, wills, and more)
*   City directories and reference indexes
*   Postcards and other archival materials
*   And various other kinds of historical archives

All collections are searchable through our search engine and filters, with access to record images when available.   
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 I don’t speak french. Can I still use the website?

Genealogy Quebec is designed to be used by both French and English speakers. The entire website is available in English, from the menus to the tutorials to the various search engines and databases. Most original documents will only be available in their original language, but they will often be accompanied by a readout of the important information contained in the record, which is available in both French and English.

 What is Genealogy Quebec?

Genealogy Quebec is a subscription-based genealogy research platform that helps you trace your family history in Quebec (and beyond). It brings many collections together in one place and helps you find ancestors faster with a powerful search engine, helpful filters, and access to original record images when available.  
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 What are the kinds of tools and documents available on Genealogy Quebec?

On Genealogy Quebec, you can access a wide range of historical and genealogical records, including:

*   Parish registers (baptisms, marriages, burials)
*   Birth, marriage, and death records
*   Census records
*   Obituaries and death notices
*   Gravestones and memorial cards
*   Notarial records (contracts, wills, and more)
*   City directories and reference indexes
*   Postcards and other archival materials
*   And various other kinds of historical archives

All collections are searchable through our search engine and filters, with access to record images when available.   
  
 Consult a detailed overview of the website’s content [at this address](https://www.genealogiequebec.com/blog/en/2024/11/13/search-engine-content-overview/).

 I don’t speak french. Can I still use the website?

Genealogy Quebec is designed to be used by both French and English speakers. The entire website is available in English, from the menus to the tutorials to the various search engines and databases. Most original documents will only be available in their original language, but they will often be accompanied by a readout of the important information contained in the record, which is available in both French and English.

## About Quebec, Canada, Vital and Church Records (Drouin Collection), 1621-1968

**General collection information**

This collection holds over thirty million records pertaining to births, baptisms, marriages, deaths, and burials in Quebec between roughly 1621 and 1968. Most of the collection relates to Catholic Church parishes, though records from other denominations are also included. The records are written primarily in French but also include English, Latin, and Italian.

**Using this collection**

Records in the collection may include the following information:

*   Name
*   Residence
*   Occupation
*   Date and place of birth
*   Date and place of baptism
*   Date and place of marriage
*   Date and place of death
*   Date and place of burial
*   Name of parents (including mother’s maiden name)
*   Father’s occupation
*   Name and occupation of spouse
*   Name of spouse’s parents

# Recensement de 1961

Ce portail présente une sélection de ressources fournissant des données pour le recensement du Canada. Vous trouverez des **tableaux de données** en différents formats.

Vous pouvez aussi accéder à la version numérisée des publications du [recensement de 1961](http://archive.org/search.php?query=mediatype%3Atexts%20AND%20collection%3Astatisticscanada%20AND%20subject%3A%22Recensement%201961%22) sur le site Internet Archive.

## Tableaux de données

Les tableaux du recensement accessibles dans cette section Web contiennent des données en format compatible avec des chiffriers électroniques (Excel) et des logiciels statistiques comme SAS et SPSS. Les données disponibles sont celles des régions métropolitaines de recensement (RMR) subdivisés en secteurs de recensement (SR).


### Informations pratiques

**Les profils cumulatifs**

On appelle profils cumulatifs les tableaux de données exhaustifs concernant toutes les régions géographiques du recensement, disponibles au format CSV ou XLS.

Pour ouvrir et lire un fichier CSV dans Excel, [consultez le guide «Ouvrir un fichier CSV avec Excel»](https://www.bibl.ulaval.ca/geostat/statistiques/CSV-guide.pdf) (PDF), conçu par l’équipe du Centre GéoStat de l’Université Laval.

**Termes et acronymes géographiques**

Pour sélectionner le tableau répondant à vos besoins, il est important de connaitre les termes et acronymes géographiques utilisés par Statistique Canada dans la diffusion de ses données.

Par exemple, au Québec, les termes «divisions de recensement (DR)» représentent les municipalités régionales de comté (MRC), tandis que les «subdivisions de recensement (SDR)» désignent les villes, villages et municipalités composant les MRC. De même, les «régions économiques (RÉ)» correspondent aux régions administratives (RA) du Québec.

Consulter la liste des termes et acronymes géographiques dans le [Dictionnaire, Recensement de la population, 1971](https://www.bibl.ulaval.ca/geostat/recensements/r1971/docu/CS12-540-1972.pdf) (PDF).

**Concepts**

Pour comprendre les concepts utilisés dans les tableaux de données, obtenir des explications et des définitions détaillées, référez-vous au [Dictionnaire, Recensement de la population, 1971](https://www.bibl.ulaval.ca/geostat/recensements/r1971/docu/CS12-540-1972.pdf) (PDF)


### Accès aux tableaux de données

Parcourez le site Web[Analyseur de recensement canadien](https://acces.bibl.ulaval.ca/login?url=http://dc1.chass.utoronto.ca/census/index.html), qui permet d’effectuer des recherches par territoire pour [accéder aux tableaux de données du recensement de 1961](http://dc1.chass.utoronto.ca.acces.bibl.ulaval.ca/census/1961_ct.html).

## Tableaux de données

Les tableaux du recensement accessibles dans cette section Web contiennent des données en format compatible avec des chiffriers électroniques (Excel) et des logiciels statistiques comme SAS et SPSS. Les données disponibles sont celles des régions métropolitaines de recensement (RMR) subdivisés en secteurs de recensement (SR).


### Informations pratiques

**Les profils cumulatifs**

On appelle profils cumulatifs les tableaux de données exhaustifs concernant toutes les régions géographiques du recensement, disponibles au format CSV ou XLS.

Pour ouvrir et lire un fichier CSV dans Excel, [consultez le guide «Ouvrir un fichier CSV avec Excel»](https://www.bibl.ulaval.ca/geostat/statistiques/CSV-guide.pdf) (PDF), conçu par l’équipe du Centre GéoStat de l’Université Laval.

**Termes et acronymes géographiques**

Pour sélectionner le tableau répondant à vos besoins, il est important de connaitre les termes et acronymes géographiques utilisés par Statistique Canada dans la diffusion de ses données.

Par exemple, au Québec, les termes «divisions de recensement (DR)» représentent les municipalités régionales de comté (MRC), tandis que les «subdivisions de recensement (SDR)» désignent les villes, villages et municipalités composant les MRC. De même, les «régions économiques (RÉ)» correspondent aux régions administratives (RA) du Québec.

Consulter la liste des termes et acronymes géographiques dans le [Dictionnaire, Recensement de la population, 1971](https://www.bibl.ulaval.ca/geostat/recensements/r1971/docu/CS12-540-1972.pdf) (PDF).

**Concepts**

Pour comprendre les concepts utilisés dans les tableaux de données, obtenir des explications et des définitions détaillées, référez-vous au [Dictionnaire, Recensement de la population, 1971](https://www.bibl.ulaval.ca/geostat/recensements/r1971/docu/CS12-540-1972.pdf) (PDF)


### Accès aux tableaux de données

Parcourez le site Web[Analyseur de recensement canadien](https://acces.bibl.ulaval.ca/login?url=http://dc1.chass.utoronto.ca/census/index.html), qui permet d’effectuer des recherches par territoire pour [accéder aux tableaux de données du recensement de 1961](http://dc1.chass.utoronto.ca.acces.bibl.ulaval.ca/census/1961_ct.html).

Open Data Portal Catalogue The open data portal catalogue is a downloadable dataset containing some key metadata for the general datasets available on the Government of Canada's Open Data portal. Resource 1 is generated using the [ckanapi tool](https://github.com/ckan/ckanapi/blob/master/README.md#bulk-dumping-and-loading) (*external link*) Resources 2 - 8 are generated using the [Flatterer](https://flatterer.opendata.coop/) (*external link*) utility. ###Description of resources: 1. [Dataset](https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/c4c5c7f1-bfa6-4ff6-b4a0-c164cb2060f7/resource/27f49273-d645-4950-9a58-c3086d833d57) is a [JSON Lines](https://jsonlines.org/) (*external link*) file where the metadata of each Dataset/Open Information Record is one line of JSON. The file is compressed with GZip. The file is heavily nested and recommended for users familiar with working with nested JSON. 2. [Catalogue](https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/c4c5c7f1-bfa6-4ff6-b4a0-c164cb2060f7/resource/b8931c16-0710-4c31-bbda-f60841e98cb4) is a XLSX workbook where the nested metadata of each Dataset/Open Information Record is flattened into worksheets for each type of metadata. 3. # Open Government Portal

About this information
Open data is defined as structured data that is machine-readable, freely shared, used and built on without restrictions.

The key things to remember about open data are:

*   #Availability and access#: the data must be available as a whole and at no more than a reasonable reproduction cost, preferably by downloading over the internet. The data must also be available in a convenient and modifiable form.
*   #Re-use and redistribution#: the data must be provided under terms that permit re-use and redistribution including the intermixing with other datasets.
*   #Universal participation#: everyone must be able to use, re-use and redistribute. There should be no discrimination against fields of endeavour or against persons or groups. For example, 'non-commercial' restrictions that would prevent 'commercial' use, or restrictions of use for certain purposes (e.g. only in education), are not allowed.

# Open Government Portal

About this information
Open data is defined as structured data that is machine-readable, freely shared, used and built on without restrictions.

The key things to remember about open data are:

*   #Availability and access#: the data must be available as a whole and at no more than a reasonable reproduction cost, preferably by downloading over the internet. The data must also be available in a convenient and modifiable form.
*   #Re-use and redistribution#: the data must be provided under terms that permit re-use and redistribution including the intermixing with other datasets.
*   #Universal participation#: everyone must be able to use, re-use and redistribute. There should be no discrimination against fields of endeavour or against persons or groups. For example, 'non-commercial' restrictions that would prevent 'commercial' use, or restrictions of use for certain purposes (e.g. only in education), are not allowed.

# Open databases



Open databases are the core component of the Linkable Open Data Environment (LODE). You can contribute to their development by reporting new publicly available datasets released by municipalities, provinces, territories or other organizations.

## Open databases released

### The Open Database of Greenhouses

[![Image 2: The Open Database of Greenhouses ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-odg.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/32-26-0005/322600052023001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Greenhouses (ODG)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/32-26-0005/322600052023001-eng.htm) version 2.0 contains approximately 3,900 manually digitized greenhouses from various open-source earth observation imagery.

In the newest version, an additional 1,006 greenhouse footprints were automatically detected and digitized using machine learning methods.

The database is in GIS (Geographic Information System) format.

Release dates:

*   August 18, 2025— Version 2.0
*   February 2, 2023 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Buildings

[![Image 3: The Open Database of Buildings ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-odb.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0001/342600012018001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Buildings (ODB)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0001/342600012018001-eng.htm) version 3.0 contains approximately 14.4 million building features compiled from hundreds of sources.

Release dates:

*   April 15, 2025 — Version 3.0
*   March 1, 2019 — Version 2.0
*   November 1, 2018 — Version 1.0

### The Canadian Pedestrian Network Database

[![Image 4: The Canadian Pedestrian Network Database ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2025-06/lode-pedestrian.png)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0004/342600042025001-eng.htm)

[The Canadian Pedestrian Network Database](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0004/342600042025001-eng.htm) is a national collection of pedestrian infrastructure compiled from 55 municipalities. Pedestrian infrastructure is classified by type into sidewalks, pedestrian paths, multi-use paths, unpaved paths, and pedestrian zones, as well as connecting infrastructure, such as crosswalks, bridges, underpasses, and stairways. Where available, surface material and width are provided.

Release date:

*   March 19, 2025 — Version 1.0

### The Canadian Public Transit Network Database

[![Image 5: The Canadian Public Transit Network Database ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2025-06/lode-public-transit.png)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0003/232600032025001-eng.htm)

[The Canadian Public Transit Network Database](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0003/232600032025001-eng.htm) is a national compilation of over 100 public transit services provided in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) and geospatial formats. The data includes service information such as stops, stop times, trips, routes, calendars, and additional information where available.

Release date:

*   January 31, 2025 — Version 1.0

### The Canadian Cycling Network Database

[![Image 6: The Canadian Cycling Network Database ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2025-06/lode-cycling.png)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0004/232600042024001-eng.htm)

[The Canadian Cycling Network Database](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0004/232600042024001-eng.htm) is a national dataset of cycling infrastructure compiled from 75 municipalities. Cycling infrastructure is standardized using the Canadian Bikeway Comfort and Safety (Can-BICS) classification system.

Release date:

*   January 30, 2025 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Educational Facilities

[![Image 7: The Open Database of Educational Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-odef.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/37-26-0001/372600012022001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Educational Facilities (ODEF)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/37-26-0001/372600012022001-eng.htm) contains addresses of educational facilities across Canada. In its current version it contains approximately 19,000 records compiled from both open sources and from publicly available data (with permission from the data owners).

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release date:

*   December 13, 2024 — Version 3.0
*   November 28, 2022 — Version 2.1
*   April 9, 2021 — Version 2.0
*   August 19, 2019 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Infrastructure

[![Image 8: The Open Database of Infrastructures ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-infrastructure.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0003/342600032023001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Infrastructure](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0003/342600032023001-eng.htm) contains data across 11 infrastructure types: electric grid, oil and gas, low carbon, bridges and tunnels, airports, ports and marinas, railways, potable water, solid waste, wastewater and stormwater, and telecommunications.

Release dates:

*   November 13,2024 — Version 2.0
*   May 8,2023 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Businesses

[![Image 9: The Open Database of Businesses ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2023-11/lode-business.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/21-26-0003/212600032023001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Businesses](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/21-26-0003/212600032023001-eng.htm) contains a variety of business information, including names, addresses, locations, industry classification, and other characteristics when supplied by the data providers.

Release date:

*   November 28, 2023 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities

[![Image 10: The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-recreation.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odrsf)

[The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities (ODRSF)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odrsf) contains the name and location of major recreational spaces and amenities across Canada (such as arenas, public pools, ski resorts, etc.). This database contains approximately 182,000 records compiled from both open and publicly available data sources.

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release date:

*   September 28, 2021 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Addresses

[![Image 11: The Open Database of Addresses ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-oda.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/oda)

[The Open Database of Addresses (ODA)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/oda) is a database of civic addresses and their geo-locations, and contains over 10 million addresses across Canada. The development of the ODA has greatly benefited from a collaboration with [OpenAddresses](https://openaddresses.io/).

These addresses will also be integrated into a new National Address Register (NAR) of residential and non-residential addresses, to be made available later this year by Statistics Canada.

Release date:

*   April 29, 2021 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Cultural and Art Facilities

[![Image 12: The Open Database of Cultural and Art Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-culture.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odcaf)

[The Open Database of Cultural and Art Facilities (ODCAF)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odcaf) contains the names, addresses, and geo-coordinates of a variety of cultural and art facilities across Canada, including museums, galleries, libraries and art centres. This database contains approximately 8,000 records compiled from both open and publicly available data sources.

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release date:

*   October 2, 2020 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Healthcare Facilities

[![Image 13: The Open Database of Healthcare Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-health.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odhf)

[The Open Database of Healthcare Facilities (ODHF)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odhf) contains the names, addresses and geo-coordinates of healthcare facilities across Canada. Facilities are classified by type. The current version (version 1.1) contains approximately 7,000 records compiled from open data sources, publicly available data, and data directly provided by sources for inclusion as open data.

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release dates:

*   August 7, 2020 — Version 1.1
*   April 17, 2020 — Version 1.0

# Open databases



Open databases are the core component of the Linkable Open Data Environment (LODE). You can contribute to their development by reporting new publicly available datasets released by municipalities, provinces, territories or other organizations.

## Open databases released

### The Open Database of Greenhouses

[![Image 2: The Open Database of Greenhouses ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-odg.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/32-26-0005/322600052023001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Greenhouses (ODG)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/32-26-0005/322600052023001-eng.htm) version 2.0 contains approximately 3,900 manually digitized greenhouses from various open-source earth observation imagery.

In the newest version, an additional 1,006 greenhouse footprints were automatically detected and digitized using machine learning methods.

The database is in GIS (Geographic Information System) format.

Release dates:

*   August 18, 2025— Version 2.0
*   February 2, 2023 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Buildings

[![Image 3: The Open Database of Buildings ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-odb.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0001/342600012018001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Buildings (ODB)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0001/342600012018001-eng.htm) version 3.0 contains approximately 14.4 million building features compiled from hundreds of sources.

Release dates:

*   April 15, 2025 — Version 3.0
*   March 1, 2019 — Version 2.0
*   November 1, 2018 — Version 1.0

### The Canadian Pedestrian Network Database

[![Image 4: The Canadian Pedestrian Network Database ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2025-06/lode-pedestrian.png)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0004/342600042025001-eng.htm)

[The Canadian Pedestrian Network Database](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0004/342600042025001-eng.htm) is a national collection of pedestrian infrastructure compiled from 55 municipalities. Pedestrian infrastructure is classified by type into sidewalks, pedestrian paths, multi-use paths, unpaved paths, and pedestrian zones, as well as connecting infrastructure, such as crosswalks, bridges, underpasses, and stairways. Where available, surface material and width are provided.

Release date:

*   March 19, 2025 — Version 1.0

### The Canadian Public Transit Network Database

[![Image 5: The Canadian Public Transit Network Database ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2025-06/lode-public-transit.png)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0003/232600032025001-eng.htm)

[The Canadian Public Transit Network Database](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0003/232600032025001-eng.htm) is a national compilation of over 100 public transit services provided in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) and geospatial formats. The data includes service information such as stops, stop times, trips, routes, calendars, and additional information where available.

Release date:

*   January 31, 2025 — Version 1.0

### The Canadian Cycling Network Database

[![Image 6: The Canadian Cycling Network Database ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2025-06/lode-cycling.png)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0004/232600042024001-eng.htm)

[The Canadian Cycling Network Database](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/23-26-0004/232600042024001-eng.htm) is a national dataset of cycling infrastructure compiled from 75 municipalities. Cycling infrastructure is standardized using the Canadian Bikeway Comfort and Safety (Can-BICS) classification system.

Release date:

*   January 30, 2025 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Educational Facilities

[![Image 7: The Open Database of Educational Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-odef.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/37-26-0001/372600012022001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Educational Facilities (ODEF)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/37-26-0001/372600012022001-eng.htm) contains addresses of educational facilities across Canada. In its current version it contains approximately 19,000 records compiled from both open sources and from publicly available data (with permission from the data owners).

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release date:

*   December 13, 2024 — Version 3.0
*   November 28, 2022 — Version 2.1
*   April 9, 2021 — Version 2.0
*   August 19, 2019 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Infrastructure

[![Image 8: The Open Database of Infrastructures ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-infrastructure.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0003/342600032023001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Infrastructure](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/34-26-0003/342600032023001-eng.htm) contains data across 11 infrastructure types: electric grid, oil and gas, low carbon, bridges and tunnels, airports, ports and marinas, railways, potable water, solid waste, wastewater and stormwater, and telecommunications.

Release dates:

*   November 13,2024 — Version 2.0
*   May 8,2023 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Businesses

[![Image 9: The Open Database of Businesses ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/2023-11/lode-business.jpg)](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/21-26-0003/212600032023001-eng.htm)

[The Open Database of Businesses](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/21-26-0003/212600032023001-eng.htm) contains a variety of business information, including names, addresses, locations, industry classification, and other characteristics when supplied by the data providers.

Release date:

*   November 28, 2023 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities

[![Image 10: The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-recreation.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odrsf)

[The Open Database of Recreational and Sport Facilities (ODRSF)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odrsf) contains the name and location of major recreational spaces and amenities across Canada (such as arenas, public pools, ski resorts, etc.). This database contains approximately 182,000 records compiled from both open and publicly available data sources.

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release date:

*   September 28, 2021 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Addresses

[![Image 11: The Open Database of Addresses ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-oda.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/oda)

[The Open Database of Addresses (ODA)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/oda) is a database of civic addresses and their geo-locations, and contains over 10 million addresses across Canada. The development of the ODA has greatly benefited from a collaboration with [OpenAddresses](https://openaddresses.io/).

These addresses will also be integrated into a new National Address Register (NAR) of residential and non-residential addresses, to be made available later this year by Statistics Canada.

Release date:

*   April 29, 2021 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Cultural and Art Facilities

[![Image 12: The Open Database of Cultural and Art Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-culture.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odcaf)

[The Open Database of Cultural and Art Facilities (ODCAF)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odcaf) contains the names, addresses, and geo-coordinates of a variety of cultural and art facilities across Canada, including museums, galleries, libraries and art centres. This database contains approximately 8,000 records compiled from both open and publicly available data sources.

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release date:

*   October 2, 2020 — Version 1.0

### The Open Database of Healthcare Facilities

[![Image 13: The Open Database of Healthcare Facilities ](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/sites/default/files/images/lode-health.jpg)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odhf)

[The Open Database of Healthcare Facilities (ODHF)](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/lode/databases/odhf) contains the names, addresses and geo-coordinates of healthcare facilities across Canada. Facilities are classified by type. The current version (version 1.1) contains approximately 7,000 records compiled from open data sources, publicly available data, and data directly provided by sources for inclusion as open data.

The database is in CSV (comma-separated values) format.

Release dates:

*   August 7, 2020 — Version 1.1
*   April 17, 2020 — Version 1.0

##### Description

This Assisted Living and Social Services (ALSS) dataset describes the monthly Income Support caseload in Alberta, including two client groups: those Expected to Work (ETW) and those who have Barriers to Full Employment (BFE). Income Support provides financial benefits to individuals and families who do not have the resources to meet their basic needs, like food, clothing, and shelter. The caseload is defined as the number of households categorized as ETW or BFE during a specific reporting period. Most commonly, this is reported as the average volume for a specific period (e.g., annually).  The composition of the caseload is made up of single individuals, lone-parent families, couples with children and couples without children. In April 2018, a breakdown of the number of caseloads by SCSS Regions was added to provide greater context. ##### Description

This Assisted Living and Social Services (ALSS) dataset describes the monthly Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH) caseload in Alberta. The AISH program provides financial and health benefits to eligible adult Albertans with a permanent medical condition that prevents them from earning a living.  Caseloads are reported as the actual volume each month and by the Alberta government’s fiscal year. Depending on an individual’s situation, some AISH benefits may also be provided for a spouse or partner and dependent children.  Monthly caseloads are also shown as a portion of the entire Alberta population; and by gender, age, primary medical condition, family composition, employment participation and six service delivery regions across the province.  For locations of AISH delivery regions, choose the Alberta Assisted Living and Social Services Regions Map within the Resources section.

##### Description

This Assisted Living and Social Services (ALSS) dataset describes the monthly Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH) caseload in Alberta. The AISH program provides financial and health benefits to eligible adult Albertans with a permanent medical condition that prevents them from earning a living.  Caseloads are reported as the actual volume each month and by the Alberta government’s fiscal year. Depending on an individual’s situation, some AISH benefits may also be provided for a spouse or partner and dependent children.  Monthly caseloads are also shown as a portion of the entire Alberta population; and by gender, age, primary medical condition, family composition, employment participation and six service delivery regions across the province.  For locations of AISH delivery regions, choose the Alberta Assisted Living and Social Services Regions Map within the Resources section.

# Data

The microdata used by CRDCN researchers come primarily from Statistics Canada Survey Master files. Increasingly, the Research Data Centres (RDCs) are repositories of administrative records from a variety of sources including tax, employment insurance, social assistance, and hospitalization records. To find out more, visit our [**Understanding Microdata**](https://crdcn.ca/understanding-microdata/) page. If you would like to have access to the data in the RDCs please visit the [**Accessing RDC Data**](https://crdcn.ca/publications-data/access-crdcn-data/) page.

To assist researchers in our Research Data Centres (RDCs), we have drafted [**two separate funding acknowledgement messages**](https://crdcn.ca/publications-data/data/publication-note/) for use with their publications. We encourage RDC researchers to use this messaging to acknowledge the substantial financial contributions of the various funders who make access to needed data possible.

For most questions, contact the Analyst at your local RDC or you can contact Statistics Canada at **[statcan.dad-apu-dad-uta.statcan@statcan.gc.ca](mailto:statcan.dad-apu-dad-uta.statcan@statcan.gc.ca)**. For questions about access, contact **[info@crdcn.ca](mailto:info@crdcn.ca)**.

# Data

The microdata used by CRDCN researchers come primarily from Statistics Canada Survey Master files. Increasingly, the Research Data Centres (RDCs) are repositories of administrative records from a variety of sources including tax, employment insurance, social assistance, and hospitalization records. To find out more, visit our [**Understanding Microdata**](https://crdcn.ca/understanding-microdata/) page. If you would like to have access to the data in the RDCs please visit the [**Accessing RDC Data**](https://crdcn.ca/publications-data/access-crdcn-data/) page.

To assist researchers in our Research Data Centres (RDCs), we have drafted [**two separate funding acknowledgement messages**](https://crdcn.ca/publications-data/data/publication-note/) for use with their publications. We encourage RDC researchers to use this messaging to acknowledge the substantial financial contributions of the various funders who make access to needed data possible.

For most questions, contact the Analyst at your local RDC or you can contact Statistics Canada at **[statcan.dad-apu-dad-uta.statcan@statcan.gc.ca](mailto:statcan.dad-apu-dad-uta.statcan@statcan.gc.ca)**. For questions about access, contact **[info@crdcn.ca](mailto:info@crdcn.ca)**.

## Sources of Data - By Subject

To expand your search, you can visit the following pages:

*   [Research Guides This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/) Search for a research guide for your discipline and see if your librarian has put together a page or section sharing data, datasets, or statistics.   
*   [Statistics Canada's subject page This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/subjects?MM=1) Pick a subject to navigate to a specialized portal or hub.   
*   [Statistics Canada's Survey by Subjects This link opens in a new window](https://www23.statcan.gc.ca/imdb-bmdi/pub/indexth-eng.htm?MM) Pick a subject to find a list of Statistics Canada surveys strongly linked with the subject.   
*   [Canadian Census Page This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/data/census) Explore the Canadian Census for data about population, age, sex, dwellings, families, marital status, language, immigration and ethnocultural diversity, aboriginal peoples, education and labour, mobility and migration, language of work, income and housing.   
*   [DLI and RDC Page This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/data/dli) Learn about the DLI and RDC programs to find and access Canadian microdata.   

#### **Business and Industry**

*   [Canadian Cluster Data This link opens in a new window](https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cmb-dgcm/poi-pi/mp.html?tpcId=341&lang=eng) Interesting data on the contribution of clusters of traded industries to regional and national economies.   
*   [Canadian Industry Statistics This link opens in a new window](https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/app/cis/search-recherche?lang=eng) Analyses industry data on many economic indicators using the most recent data from Statistics Canada   
*   [SME Benchmarking Tool This link opens in a new window](https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/financial-performance-data/en) From Industry Canada - View financial performance data by industry.   
*   [Industry Canada - Trade Data Online This link opens in a new window](http://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/tdo-dcd.nsf/eng/Home) Canada and/or provinces, and/or trading partners data for imports, exports, domestic market, manufacturing shipments, trade balance.   

#### **Economy and Finances**

*   [Bank of Canada This link opens in a new window](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/) Interest and exchange rates, price indices, monetary indicators and statistics.   
*   [Canadian Metropolitan Outlook - Halifax This link opens in a new window](https://ezproxy.library.dal.ca/login?Url=http://www.conferenceboard.ca/e-library/abstract.aspx?did=7108) Overview and forecasts for the Halifax economy from the Conference Board of Canada.   
*   [RBC Economics Research This link opens in a new window](http://www.rbc.com/economics/index.html) Provides analysis and forecasts of the Canadian economy and financial markets. Also included are the indicators for the United States and key international markets.   
*   [Finances of the Nation This link opens in a new window](https://www.ctf.ca/EN/EN/Publications/Finances_of_the_Nation_Online.aspx) From the Canadian Tax Foundation.   

#### **First Nations**

*   [Indigenous and Northern Affairs Canada - Research and Statistics This link opens in a new window](https://www.sac-isc.gc.ca/eng/1100100016570/1604594851787) Includes demographic projections, fact sheets, population by gender and residence.   
*   [First Nation Profiles This link opens in a new window](https://fnp-ppn.aadnc-aandc.gc.ca/fnp/Main/index.aspx?lang=eng) From Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada.   
*   [Focus on Geography Series 2021 This link opens in a new window](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/as-sa/fogs-spg/index.cfm?Lang=E) Data on Indigenous Peoples, Immigration and Ethnocultural Diversity, Education, Labour, Income and Housing at different levels of geography.   
*   [Indigenous Statistics Portal This link opens in a new window](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/subjects-start/indigenous_peoples) Stat Can subject portal.   

#### **Health**

*   [COVID-19: A Data Perspective This link opens in a new window](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/covid19) Statistics Canada data portal for COVID data. Explore the dashboards under "Highlights" or click on "All COVID-19 releases" for a searchable list of data tables, data publications, etc.   
*   [Canadian Alcohol and Drug Use Monitoring Survey (CADUMS) This link opens in a new window](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/health-concerns/drug-prevention-treatment/drug-alcohol-use-statistics.html) Summaries available from Health Canada, microdata available in SDA (see Canadian Datasets).   
*   [Health Statistics LibGuide This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/healthstats) For a comprehensive resource outlining the best places to find health statistics, see our LibGuide for that topic.   
*   [Statistics Canada - Health Statistics This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/subjects/Health) Portal of Statistics Canada Health Statistics.   
*   [Statistics Canada - Health Profiles - 2013 This link opens in a new window](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/health-sante/82-228/index.cfm?Lang=E&sid=a&lid=1) Use the "Browse" pull-down menu to select Nova Scotia. Explore the Health Indicators instead of the Health Profiles for more recent health data.   
*   [Statistics Canada - Health Regions This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/82-402-X) Reference maps (PDF) and boundary files (geospatial software) for health regions by province. Click on the most recent entry, select "Table of Contents".   
*   [Statistics Canada - Health Trends This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/82-213-X) Comparable time-series data for a range of health indicators from a number of sources including the Canadian Community Health Survey, Vital Statistics, and Canadian Cancer Registry (last released in 2014).   
*   [Canadian Biomonitoring Dashboard This link opens in a new window](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/biomonitoring/) "Levels of environmental chemicals in the Canadian population from the Canadian Health Measures Survey"   
*   [Physical Activity, Sedentary Behaviour and Sleep Indicators This link opens in a new window](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/pass/data-tool.html?ind=1) "A snapshot of daily movement behaviours among Canadian children, youth and adults, using the Physical Activity, Sedentary Behaviour, and Sleep (PASS) Indicators."   

#### **Housing, Income, and Poverty**

*   [CMHC Data Tables This link opens in a new window](https://www.cmhc-schl.gc.ca/professionals/housing-markets-data-and-research) These tables provide an overview of housing conditions and trends in Canada and in each province and Census Metropolitan Area, including housing construction, prices, and sales; rental market trends; mortgage lending; and housing stock.   
*   [Income Statistics This link opens in a new window](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/programs/about-canada-revenue-agency-cra/income-statistics-gst-hst-statistics.html) Annual data from the Canada Revenue Agency, including by Census Subdivision.  [more...](javascript:void(0);)[less...](javascript:void(0);)  The annual Income Statistics reports use tables of data to create a profile of Canadian taxpayers.  
  
 Final Statistics - Sample Data  
 Detailed profiles of Canadian taxfilers based on a stratified random sample of individual tax returns  
  
 Interim Statistics - Universe Data  
 Preliminary statistics based on the universe of all returns filed and processed during a given tax year. This usually represents about 97% of all returns filed   
*   [Focus on Geography Series 2021 This link opens in a new window](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/as-sa/fogs-spg/index.cfm?Lang=E) Data on Indigenous Peoples, Immigration and Ethnocultural Diversity, Education, Labour, Income and Housing at different levels of geography.   
*   [Royal LePage House Price Survey This link opens in a new window](https://www.royallepage.ca/en/realestate/info-and-advice/market-reports-and-surveys/) Comprehensive reports from Halifax to the national market. Links to data tables are provided at the end of many releases.   

#### **Immigration**

*   [Citizenship and Immigration Statistics This link opens in a new window](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/reports-statistics/statistics-open-data.html) Contains annual statistical information, quarterly administrative data releases, and a 1966 to 1996 statistics archive.   
*   [Focus on Geography Series 2021 This link opens in a new window](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/as-sa/fogs-spg/index.cfm?Lang=E) Data on Indigenous Peoples, Immigration and Ethnocultural Diversity, Education, Labour, Income and Housing at different levels of geography.   

#### **Politics, Voting and Opinion Polls**

*   [Canadian Opinion Research Archive (CORA) This link opens in a new window](https://odesi.ca/en) As of December 2017, you can download the microdata of many Canadian opinion polls in Odesi. Select "CORA" or "Public Opinion Polls" under "Collections".   
*   [Canadian Opinion Research Archive (CORA) - Canadian Election Studies and Other Polls This link opens in a new window](https://www.queensu.ca/cora/data-holdings) Why people vote the way they do ... what does and does not change during the campaign and from one election to another.   
*   [Ipsos Canada This link opens in a new window](https://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/dataverse/Ipsos) Free access to Canadian opinion polls about voting intentions and some other topics.   
*   [Odesi This link opens in a new window](https://odesi.ca/en) Dalhousie does not subscribe to Odesi, but much of its content is publicly available. It is possible to both download files and do some online data tabulations. You can use Odesi to do a variable search for Statistics Canada microdata and to download many PUMFs. Microdata from many CORA opinion polls are also available for download in Odesi. There is some added value compared to the official PUMFs distributed on Statistics Canada's website.   

#### **Transportation**

*   [North American Transportation Statistics database This link opens in a new window](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/north-american-transportation-statistics-database) Includes Canada, USA, Mexico.   
*   [Urban Transportation Indicators 2016 This link opens in a new window](https://www.tac-atc.ca/en/knowledge-centre/technical-resources-search/publications/rpt-utip5-e/) Includes indicators for several Canadian cities including Halifax.   

#### **Other**

*   [Atlantic Data Stream This link opens in a new window](https://atlanticdatastream.ca/#/) Gives access to "full water quality datasets collected by 23 monitoring groups from Newfoundland and Labrador, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia."   
*   [Canadian Astronomy Data Centre This link opens in a new window](https://www.cadc-ccda.hia-iha.nrc-cnrc.gc.ca/en/) "The CADC's data collection, along with its world-leading cloud infrastructure for astronomy, provides a unique resource for data-intensive astrophysical research."   
*   [Data on Racialized Populations This link opens in a new window](https://learn.scholarsportal.info/featured/data-on-racialized-populations/) Guide providing a "starting point for researchers investigating topics about anti-racism and the impact of racism."   
*   [National Climate Data and Information Archive This link opens in a new window](https://climate.weather.gc.ca/) "Access historical weather, climate data, and related information for numerous locations across Canada. "   
*   [National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) This link opens in a new window](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/environment/pollution-waste-management/national-pollutant-release-inventory.html) Find out about pollutant releases and transfers by postal code.   
*   [Women in Canada: A Gender-based Statistical Report: 2015 This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/89-503-x/89-503-x2015001-eng.htm) Comprehensive portrait of women in Canada today including their demographic profile, family status, health, educational attainment, labour force characteristics, and income levels, as well as their involvement in criminal activity as both perpetrators and victims.   
*   [Urban Data Centre This link opens in a new window](https://data.urbandatacentre.ca/) "The mission of the Canadian Urban Data Catalogue (CUDC) is to provide awareness of the vast array of urban and non-urban Canadian data by providing an open catalogue of Canadian datasets."   

## Tips for Citing Statistical Sources

*   [How to Cite Statistics Canada Products This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/12-591-x/12-591-x2021001-eng.htm) Statistics Canada's guides to citing Statistics Canada data. The 2021 guide includes APA examples.   
*   [Citing guide for Statistics Canada and other statistical sources This link opens in a new window](https://www.lib.sfu.ca/find/other-materials/data-gis/data/citing-statistics) Guide from Simon Fraser University's library.   
*   [Data citation: APA 7 style guide This link opens in a new window](http://hdl.handle.net/10393/40673) Guide from uOttawa's library with advanced examples such as how to cite microdata from Statistics Canada.   

## Canadian Portals

*   Alberta Open Data Portal This link opens in a new window "Search a listing of Government of Alberta open datasets."   
*   [Community Information Database This link opens in a new window](http://www.cid-bdc.ca/home) Click on "Start Mapping" or on "Get Data" to find numbers from the 2011 census. Community profiles have data from the 2006 census.   
*   [Re3Data This link opens in a new window](https://www.re3data.org/) Collections of research data including Canadian scientific and medical data sets from the National Research Council of Canada.   
*   [Open Government - Open Data Portal This link opens in a new window](https://open.canada.ca/en) Provides a "single-window" to data already published by individual departments and agencies on their public websites.   
*   [Statistics Canada - Statistics by Subject This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/subjects?MM=1) Pick a subject to navigate to a specialized portal or hub.   
*   [Statistics Canada - Surveys by Subject This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/type/surveys) Pick a subject to find a list of Statistics Canada surveys strongly linked with the subject.   

## Maps and geography

##### **GIS Centre**

Consider consulting the GIS Centre for additional help and information. See also GISciences Centre's In-house Data and the geospatial data page for more maps and geospatial data.

*   [GIS Centre This link opens in a new window](https://libraries.dal.ca/find/map-collection.html) The GIS Centre on the fifth floor of the Killam Library, provides support for Geographic Information Sciences research and teaching. It is the largest library based GISciences Centre in Canada.   
*   [GIS Centre's Internal Data This link opens in a new window](https://libraries.dal.ca/find/data/gis-internal-data.html) Collection of restricted datasets available to the Dalhousie community.   
*   [Geospatial Data page This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/data/geospatial) List of helpful resources for finding geospatial data.   

##### **Nova Scotia Only**

To expand your search, consult the [Nova Scotia section](http://dal.ca.libguides.com/c.php?g=257114&p=2984676#s-lg-box-wrapper-10815791)of the Geospatial Data page.

*   [2021 Halifax Urban Census Tract Maps This link opens in a new window](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/geo/maps-cartes/referencemaps-cartesdereference/cma_ca_ct-rmr_ar_sr/map-eng.cfm?CMA=205) Census Tract reference maps (PDFs) for Halifax from the 2021 census. Make sure to also download the inset maps.   
*   [2016 Halifax Urban Census Tract Map This link opens in a new window](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2016/geo/map-carte/ref/ct/alternative-eng.cfm?CMACA=205) Census Tract reference maps (PDFs) for Halifax from the 2016 Census. Make sure to also download the inset map.   
*   [Dal Libraries Census of Population 2016 page This link opens in a new window](https://libraries.dal.ca/find/data/census2016.html) 2016 PDF DA maps and ADA maps for Nova Scotia, and 2016 census documentation   

*   [Handout about 2016 PDF maps for Nova Scotia](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/ld.php?content_id=34791823)How to interpret the geographical codes and where to download the maps.  

*   [Explore HRM This link opens in a new window](https://data-hrm.hub.arcgis.com/pages/mapping-application) Apply layers to identify features such as fire stations, zoning, wet lands, etc.   
*   [GeoNOVA This link opens in a new window](https://geonova.novascotia.ca/) "the Province of Nova Scotia's gateway to geographic information about Nova Scotia."   
*   [Nova Scotia Civic Address File This link opens in a new window](https://geonova.novascotia.ca/civic-addressing) Searching and mapping.   

##### **Canada**

*   [2021 Census - Maps and Geography This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/data/census#s-lg-box-16439966) Collection of links to census geography products including reference (PDF) maps, boundary files (geospatial software), agriculture boundary files, etc.   
*   [Census page This link opens in a new window](https://dal.ca.libguides.com/data/census) More on census geography prior to 2021.   
*   [Scholars GeoPortal This link opens in a new window](http://geo1.scholarsportal.info/) Download boundary files from current and historical Canadian censuses.   
*   [Scholars GeoPortal - 2016 Census Tract Boundaries - Halifax example (slides and screen recordings) This link opens in a new window](https://dalu-my.sharepoint.com/:p:/g/personal/jl540955_dal_ca/EQywbiVbg2lBsC-by0RcRzAByFCmvVvt3KFr69EFe0XDIg?e=ASOyPe) Short demonstration (with no audio) on how to download a shapefile of Halifax census tracts in Scholars GeoPortal.   
*   [Health Regions This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/82-402-X) Reference maps (PDF) and boundary files (geospatial software) for health regions by province. Click on the most recent entry, select "Table of Contents".   
*   [Census of Agriculture - Reference Maps This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/en/catalogue/95-630-X) PDF maps for the census of agriculture.   

## Historical Datasets

*   [StatCan InfoGuide on Historical Resources This link opens in a new window](https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/library/historical) "This guide lists sources of historical statistics produced by Statistics Canada and its predecessor agencies."   
*   [Historical Statistics of Canada, 2nd Ed. This link opens in a new window](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/11-516-x/3000140-eng.htm) Contains about 1,088 statistical tables on the social, economic and institutional conditions of Canada from the start of the Confederation in 1867 to the mid-1970s.  [more...](javascript:void(0);)[less...](javascript:void(0);)  Two formats are offered:  
  
 * text as HTML pages and all tables as individual spreadsheets in comma separated value files (csv) (which allows online viewing or downloading)  
  
 * PDF files containing both text and tables (the 22 sections are accessible as 22 individual PDF files).   
*   [Baldwin-Green Study: Canada - U.S. Census of Industry 1867-1940 This link opens in a new window](https://hdl.handle.net/10864/10341) Canadian and US manufacturing industries at the 2-digit SIC code level for census years 1900 to 1940. The Canadian figures start at 1870.   
*   [Canada Yearbook Historical Collection This link opens in a new window](https://www65.statcan.gc.ca/acyb_r000-eng.htm) Covers the first century of Canada's history, from 1867 to 1967, with historical text, tables, charts and maps.   
*   [Canada Year Book Tables This link opens in a new window](https://www65.statcan.gc.ca/acyb02/acyb02_0000-eng.htm) Selected statistics from 1907 to 1967 at ten year intervals.   
*   [Historical Canadian Macroeconomic Dataset 1871-1994 This link opens in a new window](https://qspace.library.queensu.ca/handle/1974/7667) Includes GNP, implicit price deflator, population, real GNP, per capita GNP, government expenditures, exports, imports, money suppy, bond yields, investment expenditures, current account balance.   
*   [Inflation Calculator from 1914 to the present This link opens in a new window](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/related/inflation-calculator/) From the Bank of Canada, based on Statistics Canada's CPI data.
